objectClass.primaryType: twin-arm steel street lighting column with two cobra-head lanterns
motionPotential: none - bolted to a foundation, rigid body
objectClass.notes: Bilateral symmetry about the YZ plane (x=0) AND about the XY plane. The plate is square-framed at aspect 0.838 against the declared 0.52, so it carries the fixture and not the assembly proportions; the declared 5.2 x 10.0 x 0.4 m envelope governs.

reasoning: Two macro assemblies: the tapered column and the twin-arm lyre that carries both lanterns.

The two arms and the two lantern housings are ONE continuous member in this fixture - the lyre - so they are one tapered-sweep whose section swells at each lantern rather than four components. That is what keeps a symmetric twin-arm inside a 6 draw-call ceiling.
Two repetition systems: four baseplate bolts and two refractor bowls.
No moving parts, so one root pivot and no sockets.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate. The sub-structure is real (flare, taper, swage, two arcs, two lantern swellings, two bowls) but it is carried as localFeatures and repetition systems because every componentTree entry costs a draw call.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Two arms rising from a single collar and curving out symmetrically to 1.89 m each side.
A 0.70 m cast wedge on each arm, deepest at the spigot and tapering to the nose.
An 8-segment shaft tapering r 0.110 to 0.075, 0.22 m across at the base.
The shaft swelling to r 0.168 over the bottom 0.60 m where it meets its plate.
A band 14 mm proud at the shaft top, the joint both arms rise from.
Four proud hex bolts on a 0.40 m square plate.
Two shallow prismatic acrylic bowls hung proud of the castings.
Galvanising bloom and rust runs as a post-construction canvas tile, heaviest below the hand-hole door.
A stepped cast collar where each arm enters its luminaire.

resolvedUnknowns: Shaft facet count: polygonal in the plate, built octagonal as the sector standard. Confidence 0.7.
The far side of both lanterns and of the column is not in the single view; built as a mirror about the arm plane. Confidence 0.85.

Plate proportions contradict the declared envelope (plate aspect 0.838, declared 0.52) because the plate photographs a shorter post; the declared 5.2 x 10.0 x 0.4 m governs and the plate supplies the fixture. Confidence 0.9.

Column diameter is taken from engineering practice for a 10 m twin-arm column (0.32 m across flats at the base), not from the plate: scaling the plate by its arm span would give a 0.55 m column, which no 10 m lighting column has. Confidence 0.8.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: per-material rendered luma against the measured 141/148
turntable hole gate at 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees
both arcs read as curves on the 0-degree frame
antiShallowSpecRules: Every identity-defining detail in the inventory maps to a named localFeature, a vertexPaint region or a repetitionSystem - never to prose alone.
Every material carries a measured crop as textureless evidence.
Every geometric figure is measured off the plate, measured off the proxy band table, or derived from the declared envelope, and says which.
mustNotDo: Do not take proportion from the plate or the Meshy proxy; both carry the plate's square framing.
Do not split the lyre into four components; it is one cast member and four would break the draw-call ceiling.
Do not author a fourth material for the rust; it is a colour region on the steel.
Do not add a pivot per component or any socket.
Do not seat a refractor bowl flush with the housing underside - coincident co-facing surfaces z-fight.
qualityContract.depthRationale: FIVE components across three material layers: the column and its lyre and lantern pair as macro, the baseplate and refractor pair as meso. Nine micro-feature groups sit inside those merges -- octagonal taper, base flare, top collar, hand-hole door, twin arms, two cobra wedges, two spigot collars, four proud bolts and two refractor bowls -- separated by vertex colour rather than by extra materials.

mustMatch: reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
niceToHave: micro scratches, stains, chips, and dirt masks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

assumptions: The column is octagonal: the plate's section is polygonal rather than round, and eight sides is the sector standard. Confidence 0.7.
The far side of both lanterns and of the column is mirrored across the arm plane; the single view cannot show it. Confidence 0.85.
Column diameter is engineering-derived (0.32 m across flats at the base for a 10 m column), NOT scaled from the plate, which would give 0.55 m.

The arms and the lantern housings share one material. The measured crops differ by seven luma (141 against 148), which is a colour difference and not a material difference, and folding them saves two draw calls.
No cabling, brackets or fixings are modelled: thin geometry the budget cannot carry and the reference reconstruction loses.
Metalness is authored below a physical 1.0 on both metals because the review harness carries no environment map.
The lanterns' internal gear trays are not modelled: the kit builds exterior shells only.

componentTree.name: Tapered galvanised shaft with collar and hand-hole door
componentTree.topologyRationale: An assembled solid merged into one mesh: the flared tapered shaft, its top collar and the bolted hand-hole door share one galvanised material and one submission. Built as EIGHT segments rather than twelve because the plate's column reads octagonal; the previous build shipped a round pipe.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Origin base-center on the foundation, +Y up. A lathe flaring from r 0.168 at the plate to r 0.118 by 0.60 m, then tapering r 0.110 to 0.075 by 7.52 m, closing with a banded collar 14 mm proud over 7.54-7.72 m.

localFeatures.description: An 8-segment lathe tapering r 0.110 to 0.075 -- 0.22 m across at the base, which is the figure the asset notes give. The plate's own shaft is 0.177 of its span, which at the declared 5.2 m would be 0.92 m across: these plates photograph real lamps that are routinely not the declared size, so FORM comes from the plate and PROPORTION from the declaration.

The shaft swells over the bottom 0.60 m from r 0.118 to r 0.168 where it meets its plate. The plate's column is visibly much wider at the foot than under the collar, and the flare is most of what reads as a structural column rather than a pipe.
A band 14 mm proud over the top 0.18 m of the shaft. Both arms rise from THIS collar, which is what makes the head a lyre rather than two brackets clamped at different heights.
A bolted 0.14 x 0.40 m cover plate 4 mm proud at 1.05 m, the source of the long rust run the plate shows below it.

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 5.20 x 9.97 x 0.40 m against the declared 5.2 x 10 x 0.4 -- exact on width and depth, 0.3% under on height. Width is set by the two lantern noses at +-2.60 m and depth by the baseplate, both landed deliberately. Proportion comes from the DECLARATION, not the plate: the plate's shaft is 0.177 of its own span, which at 5.2 m would be a 0.92 m shaft against the 0.22 m the asset notes state.

Both arms rise from ONE banded collar at the shaft top and curve out symmetrically as eased quarter-turns -- tight at the top, straight along the outreach, which is the shape of a real bracket arm and what the plate shows. The previous build was two thin wires off a smooth pipe with no collar to rise from. Arm radius 0.055, below the single-arm cobra's 0.062, because a median column carries two lighter arms.

A 0.70 m cast wedge on each arm, deepest at the spigot (0.150 m) and tapering to the nose (0.086 m), each over an acrylic refractor bowl hung proud of the casting, and each with the stepped spigot collar the plate shows where the arm enters. A plain box reads as a shoebox on a stick; the taper is the cobra.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A soft key from the upper front-left: the column's left facets read brighter than its right and the lantern crowns are the brightest metal surfaces.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review harness parity - the harness key sits at (3, 5, 4).

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Shadow sides are lifted rather than black, at roughly a 0.7 shadow-to-key ratio.
No separate rim is visible in the plate - the object separates from the backdrop by value alone.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review only; the harness rim at (0, 3, -5) is a harness convention the model must not depend on.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A near-white seamless backdrop at luma ~246 fills the frame; foreground coverage is 12.2%. The review harness approximates it with a HemisphereLight(0xffffff, 0x404040, 1.6) and NO environment map, which is why every metal here is authored below metalness 1.0: a raw metal has no diffuse term and nothing to reflect, and it renders DARKER than the 58 backdrop, which the turntable gate reads as a hole punched through the model.

The review harness applies ACES filmic tone mapping, which rolls off highlights, so a painted luma reads lower than its raw value. Albedo is therefore verified in the render and corrected against the measurement rather than copied through from the crop.

Ambient occlusion is authored per material (cavityStrength 0.2, contactShadowBias 0.3) to darken joints and seams. The prop's ground shadow is the level bake's job, not the factory's - the factory sets castShadow/receiveShadow and nothing else.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
